overview: This 202-page file traces U.S. and Peruvian investigations of Japanese residents and organizations in Peru from 1945 to 1949. It focuses on Aikoku Doshi Kai’s rejection of Japan’s defeat, intimidation of dissenters, and the arrest and deportation of its organizers. Later records document Japanese mutual associations and their statutes.
interest: The file pairs allegations and investigative findings with deportation records, public defenses, and detailed postwar association statutes.
